A dedicated remote Mac mini for developers: setup, access and pricing

Reviewed: 2026-11-21 · WodeMac

A remote Mac is a real Mac in a data center that you use over the network to build, test and run software. WodeMac rents physical M6 Mac minis hosted in California, each to one customer, with admin rights and the WodeMac Remote Screen app for access from a computer, phone or iPad. Prices start at $169 a month, paid upfront.

Why developers use a dedicated remote Mac

  • You work on Windows or Linux but need Xcode for builds, simulator tests and signing.
  • You want builds and automated tests to run on a machine that stays online, not on your laptop.
  • Your team needs a US-based cloud workstation to develop and run software around the clock.
  • You teach or lead a team and want one identically configured Mac per person.

Under the WodeMac terms and Apple's macOS software license, a rented Mac is for software development and testing: developing, building, testing and running software and developer tools.

What you get

  • A physical M6 Mac mini with a 12-core CPU, 16GB unified memory and 256GB storage. Bare metal, not a VM, and not shared with other customers.
  • Hosted in California and online 24/7.
  • Admin rights, so you install the tools and versions your project needs.
  • The WodeMac Remote Screen app for remote desktop from a computer, phone or iPad.
  • Delivery usually within 24 hours of payment and no later than 3 business days.

For maintenance, WodeMac and the hosting provider keep admin access through DeskIn. Teams can order several Macs.

Connecting and first login

WodeMac helps you with the first login remotely. After that you open the Mac's desktop with WodeMac Remote Screen. If you prefer a terminal, you can turn on Remote Login (SSH) yourself in System Settings › General › Sharing.

How responsive the desktop feels depends on your own network path to California, so try it with real work early. Xcode, Homebrew and Git are not preinstalled; you install them with your admin rights.

Check it with a real project

Install your toolchain, clone a repository you are authorized to use, and run the project's existing build and tests. Note how long they take, whether the disk has room for the simulators you need, and how the remote desktop feels in Xcode.

Write down versions and setup steps as you go. That record makes the second Mac for a teammate a repeatable job, and it tells you whether to pick a longer billing period.

Pricing

Prices are per Mac in USD, paid upfront for the period you choose. They cover the machine only; the Apple Developer Program and other third-party services are billed separately under their own terms.

FAQ

Is this a virtual machine?

No. Each machine is a physical M6 Mac mini rented to exactly one customer. WodeMac and the hosting provider keep admin access for maintenance.

Is Xcode preinstalled?

Only the WodeMac Remote Screen app is guaranteed at delivery. You have admin rights, so you install Xcode, Homebrew, Git and anything else your project needs.

How fast is delivery?

Usually within 24 hours of payment, and no later than 3 business days. WodeMac helps with the first login remotely.

Can a team order several Macs?

Yes. Each Mac is rented to one customer, and teams can order several. Yearly orders of 5 or more Macs get 2.5% off the first year.
